findings.where: First screen, the blue field behind everything, at desktop and phone: the diagonal stripe pattern across the whole hero
findings.fault: The brief asks for one flat field of blue, and the tile's own Texture panel says 'No texture: one flat field, no grain and no gradient.' The hero is covered in diagonal hatching instead. The page contradicts its own spec. The stripes make the field busy behind the white type and the portrait, and the hatching looks like a drafting or tech pattern, not a calm colour field.
findings.who_objects: The founder judges this first screen first and asked for 'refined', 'nothing in-your-face techy' and at most one quiet ground. Seeing a ground the specimen says isn't there also undercuts the specimen. Mark has called busy sites 'much too busy'.

findings.where: First screen, the oversized pale 'PPP' watermark behind the heading (desktop, behind lines 1–3); on phone it is cropped to a stray 'PP' shape beside the heading's right edge
findings.fault: A second decorative layer sits behind the one large line and competes with it. When you squint, the headline's first lines read as text over a blurred glyph block. On the phone the crop leaves a shape you can't read, which looks like a rendering fault. A giant ghosted acronym is also a stock consultancy trick, which goes against the brief's 'scale contrast, not more elements'.
findings.who_objects: The founder wants one very large serif line with nothing added, and refined, not novelty. A development-bank visitor's eye snags on the ghost letters before reading Mark's sentence.

findings.where: Article specimen: the image caption, the 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?' subhead, the three-item list and the PDF row under it, at desktop and phone
findings.fault: The specimen was there to prove the rhythm survives added content, and it fails at each place content was added. The subhead sits right under the caption with almost no space, so it groups with the photo above, not the text it heads. The list is set much tighter than the paragraphs and its lines nearly touch. The rule and the PDF row press against the last list item. The reading column falls apart just where Angélique would add an image, a subhead and a list.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the brief makes this the test: 'the look must survive Angélique's content', shown in this specimen. A reader of Mark's articles, who sees a cramped, unfinished page where the article is the product.

findings.where: First screen at phone width: the order nav, portrait, heading, lead, labels, then the address button
findings.fault: The portrait fills almost the whole first phone screen. Mark's line starts low on that screen, and the one action, the address, is pushed down to the second screen. On a phone, the first screen gives a photo and part of a sentence, but no way to reach him.
findings.who_objects: A development-agency visitor opening the link from LinkedIn on a phone, who sees no route to Mark without scrolling. It also breaks the brief's 'one message and one action on the first screen'.

findings.where: First screen, desktop: the overall arrangement, with text in a left column and the studio portrait as a plain rectangle in a right column
findings.fault: Without the stripes, this is the stock split hero: a headline left and a boxed head-and-shoulders photo right. The portrait's grey studio backdrop sits as a separate pale rectangle on the blue, not 'set into the field'. Many consultancies could have this layout, and it is the 'template split' the brief told v4 to avoid from round 1. The direction's lever, one blue field, carries no idea of its own.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who said v5 had 'fine parts put together dully' and asked for 'alive, not boring' and a look no consultancy could own.

findings.where: Motion sketch panel at phone width, compared with the phone hero and the desktop sketch
findings.fault: On the phone the sketch puts the portrait left and the line right, but the real phone hero stacks the portrait above the line, and the desktop sketch puts the line left. The sketch shows an entrance for a layout that exists at neither width.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who reads the motion sketch to judge how the hero will enter and is shown an arrangement the page doesn't have.
